reported_results.text: Participants with limited physical function improved in PCS, Physical Functioning (PF), and GH with tirzepatide versus semaglutide (p ≤ 0.025).
All domain scores improved (p ≤ 0.008), with greater improvements in General Health (GH) with tirzepatide versus semaglutide (5.45 vs. 4.20; p = 0.003).
However, MCS scores did not show significant improvements from baseline (p > 0.05 for both treatment arms).
At Week 72, PCS scores improved from baseline with both treatments (p < 0.001).
At Week 72, statistically significant improvements from baseline in SF-36v2 scores were observed across all domains (p < 0.001 with tirzepatide and p ≤ 0.002 with semaglutide) (Figure 2A).

Furthermore, PCS scores significantly improved from baseline with tirzepatide and semaglutide at Week 72 (p < 0.001, both treatment groups) and did not differ between groups (0.70 [ 0.03, 1.44]; p = 0.061) (Figure 1B).
